query: Platinum-group metals can promote distinct reactions, and earlier PGM-based nanoscale catalysts showed strong activity, selectivity, and durability in complex catalysis. A representative catalyst was reported to perform particularly well in ethanol oxidation, which involves 12-electron and 12-proton transfers, but these performance reports did not establish a comprehensive causal explanation of its behavior during operation. Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis explaining what governs its catalytic activity, selectivity, or durability and why. Define an unnamed controlled change with a suitable baseline, the predicted observations, the reaction regime in which the hypothesis should apply or fail, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive falsification outcome.

generation.hypothesis: Optimized d-band center combined with local coordination modulation in high-entropy PGM alloys precisely tunes the adsorption energies of ethanol and its intermediates to drive a 12-electron oxidation mechanism.
generation.material_initial_state: A nanoscale catalyst composed of platinum-group metals in a high-entropy alloy configuration featuring a random, mixed-d-element surface.
generation.intervention: Systematically adjust the proportion of a selected non-precious metal to induce a predictable shift in the d-band center and local coordination environment.
generation.conditions: Ethanol oxidation carried out under standard fuel cell operational conditions (acidic or alkaline electrolyte at designated operating potentials).
generation.structural_mediator: A combination of d-band center modulation and induced lattice strain from multi-element mixing.
generation.mechanism: The tailored alloy configuration produces a broadened distribution of electronic states. A moderate shift (approximately 0.1 eV) in the d-band center, verified by in situ spectroscopic methods, optimizes the adsorption/desorption balance for key ethanol oxidation intermediates, thereby enhancing the kinetics of the 12-electron/12-proton transfer reaction.
generation.predicted_outcome: A measured shift in the d-band center will correlate directly with increased turnover frequency and improved selectivity, as demonstrated by a higher ethanol oxidation rate compared to the baseline catalyst.
generation.baseline: Catalytic performance data of the reported high-entropy PGM catalyst for ethanol oxidation under identical conditions.
generation.boundary: This mechanism holds when the catalyst maintains a homogeneous, high-entropy solid solution; if phase segregation or significant ordering occurs, the predicted d-band modulation and its benefits will be lost.
generation.uncertainty: Although d-band center modulation is established, the precise quantitative relationship between a 0.1 eV shift and improved catalytic metrics in these HEAs remains to be refined.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of catalysts with controlled alloy composition variations that yield distinct d-band center positions. Employ in situ XPS/UPS to quantify the d-band shifts and measure ethanol oxidation activity through cyclic voltammetry.
measurements: d-band center position from spectroscopic analysis
Ethanol oxidation current density and selectivity by electrochemical testing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If altering the alloy composition does not result in measurable shifts in the d-band center or if the observed shifts do not correlate with a significant change in ethanol oxidation performance, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The research and development within the initiative of green energy and sustainability is ongoing and requires intensive exploration along multiple fronts:, e.g., physics, chemistry, material science, etc. The increasing trend in hydrogen economy investments is evident improving the aspects of hydrogen production as well as the realms of hydrogen transportation and storage. In our work, we attract the community attention to the new fast characterization method requiring small amount of sample to test material affinity of reaction with hydrogen. We introduce the method and apply it to the industrial and novel materials, such as high entropy alloys, and give a qualitative report for individual material affinity to hydrogen. We provide a comprehensive experimental evidence illustrating importance of composition in correlation with absorbed hydrogen content. Considering the PGM HEAs we indicate an intriguing fact of their low hydrogen affinity despite large atomic radii of constituent atoms. The complex PGM alloys have already many potential applications, including the field of catalysis.[ , ,  ] Supplementary to previous works, our study introduces a fresh perspective. It demonstrates

However, due to the heterogeneity of the surface atoms in HEAs, the catalytic properties of HEAs might be not limited by one principle element anymore and the d-band center theory might not be able to describe the activity of HEAs. The neighbouring active sites with different local electronic structures in HEAs also provide the possibility for tuning the selectively in complex reactions. For example, Yao et al. reported that PdPtRhRuCe HEA nanoparticles (NPs) showed almost 100% selectivity towards ammonia synthesis while the phase-separated alloy only had less than 20% selectivity. We have found that IrOsPtPdRhRu could catalyse ethanol oxidation with a 12-electron process, although the single metals generally prompt a four-electron process at most. Löffler et al. found that Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni complex solid solution showed at least comparable catalytic activity to Pt in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), in despite that none of its constituents had good ORR activity. In addition to HEA, other alternative denominations have also been discussed elsewhere, such as complex solid solutions, multiprincipal element alloys, polyelemental particles, multi-elemental alloy, and multimetallic cluster
